body.p: Reconsideration of the application and claims in light of the foregoing amendments and following remarks/arguments is respectfully requested. Status of the Claims
Claims 1-12 are currently pending in the present application.
In the Office Action, claims 1-12 were rejected.
The present Response amends claims 1-3, 5, 6, 10, and 12 and adds new claims 13 and 14. No new matter has been added.
Upon entry of these amendments, claims 1-14 will be pending. Objections to the Claims

Claims 1, 2, 5, and 12 were objected to for containing informalities. Claims 1,2, 5, and 12 have now been amended to correct these informalities. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the objection to claims 1, 2, 5, and 12 is therefore respectfully requested. Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 4 112
Claims 3, 6, and 10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter regarded as the invention.
In view of the foregoing amendments, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections of claims 3, 6, and 10 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) is respectfully requested. Rejections under 35 U.S.C. & 103
Claim 1 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over AT508274 Al by Leitl ("Leitl") in view of US 20170234134 Al by Bunker ("Bunker");

Claims 2-5 and 11-12 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over Leitl in view of Bunker and further in view of either one of US 20170167510 Al by Berschback et al. ("Berschback") or US 20110073710 Al by Rawlings et al. ("Rawlings");

Claim 6 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over Leitl in view of Bunker and in view of either one of Berschback or Rawlings, and further in view of "Processing Guidelines: ORAFOL® Films for Aircraft Applications" (ORAFOL); and
Claims 7-10 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over Leitl, Bunker and either one of Berschback or Rawlings, and further in view of US 20110262705 Al by Gupta et al. ("Gupta").

Independent claim 1 of the present application recites "locating at least one coherent field in the developed surface segment having local flow directions readable at the flow lines in a predetermined angle range around a main flow direction of the respective field." Support for this feature can be found, for example, in paragraph [0020] of U.S. Patent App. Pub. No. US 2023/0348046 (hereinafter "published specification").
For example, FIG. 3 of the present application (shown below) illustrates an

embodiment of the present invention for developing a surface segment 3 that is depicted with flow lines 4 and the positions 6 of the rivets which comprises the region 2 to be provided with aerodynamically functional film. See published specification, paragraph [0052]. For the region 2, fields 10, 20, 30, and 40 are determined such that local flow directions readable at the flow lines 4 deviate by less than + 5° from a main flow direction predetermined for each field 10, 20, 30, and 40. See published specification, paragraph [0053].

computer model of a body around which flow occurs to form a two-dimensional surface. This enables one to locate at least one coherent field having a local main flow direction, where local flow directions are readable at the flow lines in a predetermined angle range around the main flow direction of the respective field. While a surface segment may be predefined, the at least one coherent field is determined by the features of the claims. As described in paragraph [0031] of the published specification - a reduction of the wall shear stress is provided even if the flow direction of the overflow slightly deviates entirely or only in sections from the main flow direction. This deviation is permissible and can be taken into consideration by the predetermined angle range corresponding to the properties of the aerodynamically functional film of the current claims. See published specification, paragraph [0031].
It is respectfully submitted that Leitl and Bunker, alone or in combination, fail to

disclose or suggest the foregoing feature of claim 1. For example, the Office Action admits that Leitl does not specifically teach that "the at least one coherent field in the developed surface segment has local flow directions readable at the flow lines in a predetermined angle range around a main flow direction of the respective field." See Office Action, page 5. The Office Action instead relies on Bunker as allegedly suggesting this feature. See Office Action, page 5. To emphasize the differences between the above recited feature of claim 1 and Leitl, Leitl is directed to a method to optimize the micro structuring of a complex surface of a body in a flow to reduce drag. See Leitl, page 8, lines 23-27. The method of Leitl aims to cover all relevant parts of a body in a flow with a single uninterrupted film. See Leitl, page 8, lines 23- 27. However, Leitl, and the cited portions of Leitl, are silent as to locating or identifying a coherent field let alone with the conditions required by the above recited feature of claim 1 (e.g. "having local flow directions readable at the flow lines in a predetermined angle range around a main flow direction of the respective field"). Instead, as described above, Leitl merely describes a single field that represents the complete surface of a body.

It is respectfully submitted that Bunker fails to remedy the deficiencies of Leitl noted above. For example, FIG. 5 of Bunker, shown below, depicts a view of a plurality of riblets 128 on a flowpath surface 126that extend in a first longitudinal direction , which may be a downstream direction. See Bunker, paragraphs [0039] and [0040]. Bunker describes a component section, which can be a rotor blade of an aircraft engine that comprises a plurality

of riblets 128. Bunker further describes that the riblets 128 are usually uniformly disposed and therefore do not correspond ideally to local flow conditions. See Bunker, paragraph [0003]. Bunker also describes that the riblets 128 should have a non-uniform geometry and/or a non- uniform distance.

However, the features of Bunker fail to also disclose or suggest the locating of at least one coherent field with the conditions similar to Leitl. For example, Bunker appears to only describe a system that designs riblets according to local flow conditions. But these riblets are not designed uniformly inside a coherent field that is characterized by having a main flow direction and local flow directions which are readable in a predetermined angle range around the main flow direction as recited in claim 1. Bunker instead aims to use additive manufacturing to define nearby arbitrary surfaces and as such there is no need for Bunker to rely on uniform structures in certain coherent fields. See Bunker, paragraph [0009]. Even if one accepted that Bunker provided a reasoning for one of skill in the art to venture from the teachings of Leitl to Bunker, the features of Bunker would not lead that person to arrive at the above recited feature of claim 1.

As discussed above, it is respectfully submitted that Leitl and Bunker do not disclose or suggest the foregoing feature of claim 1. It is respectfully submitted that Berschback, Rawlings, ORAFOL, and Gupta fail to remedy the deficiencies of Leitl and Bunker noted above.

Because the combination of Leitl and Bunker fails to disclose or suggest at least the above-recited features of independent claim 1, the combination of Leitl and Bunker cannot render claim 1 or any of its dependent claims as obvious. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of claims 1-12 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 based on Leitl in combination with Bunker is respectfully requested.
New claims 13 and 14 ultimately depend from independent claim 1. It is therefore

respectfully submitted that new claims 13 and 14 are allowable over the cited prior art for at least the same reasons as claim 1, discussed above. Support for the new claims can be found,for example, in paragraphs [0029] and [0036] of the published specification. It is further
respectfully submitted that claims 13 and 14 recite features which further distinguish the present invention from the cited prior art.

Applicant believes that all issues raised by the Office have been addressed and that the present application is allowable for the foregoing reasons. If there are any remaining issues which the Office believes could be resolved through either a Supplemental Response or an Examiner's Amendment, Applicant respectfully invites the Office to call the telephone contact at the number indicated below.
